title: Rigatoni alla Norcina
subtitle: Rigatoni with Italian sausage, cream, and black truffle
excerpt: Rigatoni alla norcina is from Norcia in Umbria, a town famous for its pork butchers and black truffles. The sauce is Italian sausage, cream, white wine, and: in the proper version: black truffle. Even without truffle, the sausage and cream combination is a deeply satisfying pasta that takes 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla norcina is the flagship dish of Norcia (Perugia), Umbria, named for the Norcini: the travelling pork butchers of Norcia who were famous throughout Italy for their cured meats and salumi. The classic version uses fresh pork sausage and black truffle from the Norcia mountains.

content.text: Rigatoni alla norcina is an Umbrian pasta from the mountain town of Norcia: a cream sauce made with crumbled Italian sausage, white wine, and Parmigiano Reggiano. The traditional version includes fresh black truffle shaved over the finished dish. Without truffle it is still an excellent pasta; with it, it is extraordinary. Use the best Italian pork sausage you can find: the fennel seed and spice in a good sausage gives the sauce its character.

Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the crumbled sausage meat and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes until well browned. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the white wine and let it bubble and reduce for 2 minutes. Pour in the double cream. Simmer for 5 to 6 minutes until slightly reduced and the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Season well.

Cook the rigatoni in well-salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain. Add the rigatoni to the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Toss over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in most of the Parmigiano Reggiano. Serve topped with remaining cheese and fresh truffle shaved over the top if using.

items.symptom: Sauce is too rich and cloying
items.cause: Too much cream relative to the sausage
items.fix: Use only 200 ml cream for 400 g sausage and balance with pasta water at the tossing stage. The starchy water lightens the sauce.

items.symptom: Sausage is grey and steamed rather than browned
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or overcrowded, causing the meat to steam
items.fix: Brown in batches over high heat. The browning adds a caramel note that the sauce depends on.

items.symptom: Pasta absorbs all the sauce and looks dry
items.cause: Sauce reduced too far before the pasta was added
items.fix: Add pasta water generously at the tossing stage and toss quickly. Cream sauces tighten fast once off the heat.

content.text: Norcia is a small walled town in south-east Umbria. It gave Italy the word norcino, meaning pork butcher. The town is also the centre of the Italian black truffle trade from the Valnerina forests. The truffle season runs from late November to early March. During that time the dish is served in every restaurant in the region with fresh truffle shaved at the table. Outside Umbria, the version without truffle is a good weeknight pasta.
